We said stuff like this in Canada at one point - "that law is ridiculous! it will never pass!".

Then one day we woke up to find that it had not only been banned in TV commercials, but airplanes, every business (including bars), restaurants, near any doorway to a business within 10 meters, and most other public places. It's also illegal to have any marketing on cigarettes to indicate what kind they are (ex: smooth, rich, light, etc) and now individual products must be referenced to by brand and colour (ex: players brown, blue, red). They can't be on any kind of display in the store. Then they instituted a massive luxury/health tax that more than doubled the cost.

Don't get me wrong, smoking is pretty damn bad for you, and I definitely agree with some of these rules. It's essentially rolling the dice on an early death. The takeaway here is that it can hit the point of ridiculousness rapidly while you're not looking because people who spend all their time complaining about things that don't impact them are often seen as harmless and ignored. The truth is it only takes a few key politicians to say "hey, that sure would make me look good in the next election" and it all goes to shit.
